prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Transport Through Time; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: A selected factual history followed by contemporary transport comparisons. Historical pictures are reconstructions, not a claim that all countries changed at once. Plain practical clothes only; no flags, religious buildings, political events or cultural costumes. Cart: brown wooden four-wheel wagon, one healthy bay horse and adult driver in plain gray shirt and dark trousers. Steam train: black early passenger steam locomotive with red wheels and two brown wooden coaches. Early motor car: dark-green open four-wheel gasoline car with adult driver. Early aircraft: plain cream single-propeller biplane. Modern train: white electric passenger train with blue band and overhead wire. Jet: white twin-engine passenger jet with teal tail. No named cast or brand logos.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Horse-drawn brown wagon; Early black steam train; Early dark-green motor car; Cream early propeller biplane; Modern white-blue electric train; Modern white-teal passenger jet
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Opening selected pre-motor travel methods, not one universal place or date.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Three-part historical comparison diagram: adults carry baskets while walking along a path at left; adult rides a horse at center; two adults row a small wooden boat on river at right. Plain practical clothing; separate valid surfaces, not one unsafe mixed path. No engines or modern wires.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions. Reference-sheet override: any lettering requested by the opening page brief belongs only in that finished page. Keep this production reference board entirely unlabelled; no letters, numbers or pseudo-writing.

visualReview.note: Historical and modern vehicle designs and ordinary adults lock consistent recurring visual subjects; no single worldwide adoption date implied. Producer independently inspected the final installed WebP natively; complete final sequence and relevant native diagrams were independently reviewed.
